name: sqrt
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Computes root = floor(sqrt(x)) for a DW-bit unsigned input x, together with the remainder rem = x - root*root, where DW must be even, root is DW/2 bits, and rem is DW/2+1 bits. The remainder always satisfies 0 <= rem <= 2*root so that root*root + rem == x holds exactly. The circuit is a sequential digit-by-digit (non-restoring) square root: a one-hot weight bitm sweeps from 4^(DW/2-1) down to 4^0, one position per clock, and each cycle the running remainder is trial-compared against res + bitm and, when it fits, that amount is subtracted and the result bit is set. The datapath is a single add plus a compare/subtract and two shifts -- no multiplier and no memory. A pulse on in_valid latches x and starts iteration, busy is high while iterating, and out_valid pulses for one cycle when root/rem are valid; latency is DW/2 cycles per operation. Default DW = 32.
key_decisions: Digit-recurrence (digit-by-digit non-restoring) square-root algorithm, producing one result digit per clock cycle.
Multiplier-free and memory-free datapath: a single DW-bit adder/subtractor plus comparator and two shifts (0 DSP, 0 BRAM).
Latency is DW/2 cycles per operation; throughput is one result every DW/2 cycles.
Three DW-bit registers (num, res, bitm) hold the running remainder, result, and one-hot weight; a one-hot bitm sweeps from 4^(DW/2-1) down to 4^0.
Valid/busy handshake: in_valid pulse latches x and starts, busy marks iteration, out_valid pulses one cycle on completion.
Parameterized fixed-point widths: DW must be even, root is DW/2 bits, rem is DW/2+1 bits, with the invariant root*root + rem == x and rem <= 2*root.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: B. Parhami, Computer Arithmetic: Algorithms and Hardware Designs, square-root chapter (digit-by-digit / digit-recurrence square root).
Classic binary non-restoring shift-subtract square-root method (one result digit per cycle, add/compare/subtract datapath).
